title: ecmp_cost.dem t23 comment claims mid-edge packets on r1->host2/r2->host2 that the blessed capture does not show
detail: Pixel-diff of goldens/ecmp_cost/01150ms.png vs 01450ms.png shows packets only AT nodes m1/res/r1/r2/res2; none renders mid-edge; no packet is on r2->host2 at t23 (hash picks r1,r1,r2,r2; wide legs never render mid-edge at capture boundaries).
recommended_fix: Rewrite the t23 comment to describe the actual capture (packets queued at m1/res/r1/r2/res2, both paths live, none on narrow legs), or move the capture to a tick where the claimed mid-edge states exist.

title: ecmp_cost.dem places diamond B's sink at grid x=48 — outside the 40-tile map, cropped from every T2 capture
detail: Map is 40×30 tiles, window 1280×720: host2 renders at x=1312, off-screen; the blessed PNGs contain no host2 pixels and both second-hop legs clip at the window edge, so the tie-split captures cannot show the legs' far halves.
recommended_fix: Shift diamond B left (or shrink the grid spread) so host2 and the full second-hop legs fall inside the 40-tile map and the capture window.

title: Frozen spec says edge cost = representative pipe's tier cost; code prices mixed-tier bundles at min member cost
evidence:
Dijkstra over integer pipe costs (edge cost = representative pipe's tier
   `cost` via `Topology.pipe_tier` → catalog; the representative is the
   lowest-slot live pipe toward the neighbor — matches `Hop.pipe`). Array-

					min_cost[ns] = c // a fatter (cheaper) member re-prices the edge
detail: Code prices a mixed-tier bundle at the fattest member (min member cost, matching decision-log/arch), so when the lowest-slot member is narrower, the edge cost differs from the representative's tier cost — spec wording contradicts the implemented model.
recommended_fix: Reword the spec line: edge cost = the MINIMUM tier cost among live pipes toward the neighbor (fattest member); the lowest-slot representative pipe only records Hop.pipe.

title: No upper bound on tier cost — pathological ladder values overflow the i32 dist accumulation in the Dijkstra
detail: Cost is validated only >= 1; a ladder value near i32 max passes load and multi-hop dist sums wrap negative, corrupting the min-scan (UNREACHABLE = -1 sentinel). Documented as deferred in deferred-work.md; shipped ladder 20/10/5 is safe.
recommended_fix: Add the deferred upper-bound validation (e.g. cost <= 1e6) at catalog load, or clamp accumulated dist sums; acceptable as-is only while the ladder stays small.
